title: The carbon dioxide far wing rules
description: What the 25 cm-1 line cutoff of the infrared k-tables leaves out of a dense carbon dioxide air (GEN.1019, docs/design/composition/line-opacity.md). The wing of every carbon dioxide band is the Lorentz tail of its lines times the sub-Lorentzian factor chi of Perrin and Hartmann 1989 (JQSRT 42, 311), from the cutoff out to a reach. The parameters of chi are the HELIOS-K files chiPH89__CO2-CO2.dat and chiPH89__CO2-N2.dat; the band strengths are the k-tables' own, not stored here. Every number carries its source tier (T1 to T9) and tweak level (L0 to L4).

cutoff_cm1.basis: The distance from a line centre at which the ExoMolOP k-tables cut every line (physics/line_opacity.py); the wing starts where the tables stop, so nothing is counted twice

reach_cm1.basis: How far from a line the wing is carried: Simonetti and others 2021 (arXiv 2110.11702, appendix step 1, read) use the Perrin and Hartmann chi factors truncated at 500 cm-1 for carbon dioxide dominated air and say proposed truncations run from 120 cm-1 to none; their other option is 350 cm-1 with the Tonkov 1996 chi. The widest range of the two in question is 120 cm-1 to the whole grid, which the tests sweep

temperature_low_k.basis: The coolest temperature the chi parameters are used at (colder is held at this value): Perrin and Hartmann measured near 190 to 800 K (Wordsworth, Forget and Eymet 2010, read); the exponential form would give a chi above 1 for B1 under about 140 K

temperature_high_k.basis: The warmest temperature of the chi parameters' measurements (as above); hotter air holds the 800 K value, so the wing of a hot atmosphere is a lower bound

gamma_self_cm1_atm.basis: The Lorentz half width of a carbon dioxide line broadened by carbon dioxide at 296 K and one atmosphere: HITRAN's values for the strong lines of the 4.3 and 15 micron bands lie near 0.09 to 0.11 (recalled, not read); the wing goes as this width

gamma_foreign_cm1_atm.basis: The same broadened by nitrogen or air (HITRAN air broadening of the strong lines is near 0.07, recalled, not read); every gas that is not carbon dioxide takes the nitrogen value and its chi

gamma_exponent.basis: The width goes as (296 K / T) to this power (the HITRAN air exponent of the strong carbon dioxide lines is near 0.7, recalled, not read)

minor_gamma_cm1_atm.basis: The Lorentz half width at 296 K and one atmosphere of a line of a minor gas broadened by carbon dioxide: water 0.13 (HITRAN's CO2 broadening of water lines is above its air value of about 0.09, recalled), sulfur dioxide 0.10, carbon monoxide 0.065 (recalled, not read); none was found in an open source. The widest range of the two in doubt is the knob of its registry row

minor_uses_chi.basis: Whether the minor gases take the carbon dioxide self factor chi: 1 yes (the same collision partner, no minor-gas factor was found), 0 for a pure Lorentz tail. Real water wings are stronger than Lorentz in windows (the continuum), so 1 is a lower bound

chi_co2_co2.basis: Perrin and Hartmann 1989, carbon dioxide in carbon dioxide: chi is 1 up to sigma1, then falls as exp(-b1 (d - sigma1)), exp(-b1 (sigma2 - sigma1) - b2 (d - sigma2)) and the same with b3 beyond sigma3, with b_i(T) = alpha_i + beta_i exp(-epsilon_i T) per cm-1. The numbers are second-hand: the HELIOS-K file chiPH89__CO2-CO2.dat (github.com/exoclime/HELIOS-K, read 10-30), whose form Simonetti and others 2021 print as their equations 12 to 15. The paper itself was not opened

chi_co2_n2.basis: Perrin and Hartmann 1989, carbon dioxide in nitrogen, same form and same second-hand source (chiPH89__CO2-N2.dat)
